subject: Biology
description: Heart anatomy: chambers, valves, double circulation, ECG

questions.stem: The HUMAN HEART has how many chambers?
questions.explanation: Human heart = 4 chambers: 2 ATRIA (upper, receive blood) + 2 VENTRICLES (lower, pump blood out). Right side handles DEOXYGENATED blood (body → lungs); Left side handles OXYGENATED blood (lungs → body). 4-chamber design = COMPLETE separation of oxygenated + deoxygenated blood; allows DOUBLE CIRCULATION + high O₂ delivery. FISH = 2 chambers (one atrium + one ventricle). FROGS / REPTILES = 3 chambers (incomplete septum in ventricle). MAMMALS + BIRDS = 4 chambers.

questions.stem: The 'PACEMAKER' of the heart, generating the heartbeat rhythm, is the:

options.option_text: SA node (Sinoatrial node, in right atrium)
Bundle of His, in the heart wall

questions.explanation: SA NODE (Sinoatrial node) — small group of specialised cardiac cells in upper RIGHT ATRIUM. Spontaneously generates electrical impulses ~70-80 times/minute → atria contract. Signal then passes to AV NODE (Atrioventricular node, between atria + ventricles), then BUNDLE OF HIS (in interventricular septum), then PURKINJE FIBRES (spread through ventricle walls) → ventricles contract. ARTIFICIAL pacemaker — implanted device replicating SA node when natural one fails. CARDIAC arrhythmia → various nodes / conduction issues.

questions.stem: Which is the LARGEST artery in the human body?
questions.explanation: AORTA — largest ARTERY in the body (~2-3 cm diameter); carries oxygenated blood from LEFT VENTRICLE to all of body via branches. AORTA branches: ascending aorta (coronary arteries to heart muscle), aortic arch (carotid → head, subclavian → arms), thoracic aorta (chest), abdominal aorta (organs, then bifurcates into iliacs → legs). The LARGEST VEIN is the INFERIOR VENA CAVA. PULMONARY ARTERY is unusual: it's the only artery carrying DEOXYGENATED blood (right ventricle → lungs). PULMONARY VEIN is the only vein carrying OXYGENATED blood (lungs → left atrium).

questions.stem: DOUBLE CIRCULATION in mammals refers to:

options.option_text: Two atria with one ventricle pumping
Blood flowing in two directions same time

questions.explanation: DOUBLE CIRCULATION — blood passes through heart TWICE per complete circuit. (1) PULMONARY CIRCUIT: right ventricle → pulmonary artery → LUNGS (gas exchange) → pulmonary vein → left atrium. (2) SYSTEMIC CIRCUIT: left ventricle → aorta → BODY tissues (O₂ delivered) → vena cavae → right atrium. Advantage: high BP for body delivery + lower BP for delicate lung capillaries. DISCOVERED by William HARVEY (1628, 'De Motu Cordis'). Single circulation: fish (heart → gills → body → heart, only 1 pass).

questions.explanation: ECG / EKG — records ELECTRICAL impulses generated by the heart's pacemaker (SA node) + conduction system, via electrodes on skin. Shows: P wave (atrial depolarisation), QRS complex (ventricular depolarisation), T wave (ventricular repolarisation). Detects: arrhythmias, MI (myocardial infarction = heart attack), cardiac hypertrophy, ischaemia. Inventor: Willem EINTHOVEN (Dutch, Nobel 1924). Distractor 1 = echocardiogram (ultrasound) measures mechanical activity. Distractor 3 = pulse oximeter. Distractor 4 = blood test for ANP, BNP.

questions.stem: Normal HUMAN HEART RATE at rest is approximately:
questions.explanation: Normal adult resting heart rate = 60-100 bpm. Athletes often <60 (BRADYCARDIA — physiological in athletes; pathological if causing symptoms). >100 = TACHYCARDIA. Newborns: 100-160 bpm. Children gradually slow down. During exercise → up to 180+ in younger adults. Maximum HR ≈ 220 − age (rough rule). HEART pumps ~5 L/min at rest (CARDIAC OUTPUT = stroke volume × HR). Heart contracts ~3 BILLION TIMES in average lifetime.

questions.stem: Which valve prevents BACKFLOW of blood from the LEFT VENTRICLE into the LEFT ATRIUM?

options.option_text: Pulmonary semilunar valve at lung side
Aortic semilunar valve at aorta side

questions.explanation: 4 HEART VALVES — prevent backflow: (1) TRICUSPID (3 cusps) — between RIGHT atrium + RIGHT ventricle. (2) MITRAL / BICUSPID (2 cusps) — between LEFT atrium + LEFT ventricle. (3) PULMONARY SEMILUNAR (3 cusps) — between right ventricle + pulmonary artery. (4) AORTIC SEMILUNAR (3 cusps) — between left ventricle + aorta. Mnemonic: 'Try Pulling My Aorta' (right to left). Mitral valve issues are common: stenosis (narrow), regurgitation (leaky), prolapse. Mitral valve replacement is a major cardiac surgery.
